item.title: 38 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry
item.description: There are 38 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry today. That’s according to figures from the Irish Nurses’ and Midwives’ Organisation. They show there are 21 patients waiting on a trolley in UHK’s emergency department, while a further 17 people are waiting on trolleys in wards within the hospital. item.title: Bluetongue virus may cause fewer mortalities in Ireland than other parts of Europe
item.description: It’s hoped that the bluetongue disease will be less severe in Ireland than it has been in other parts of Europe. Avril Hobson is Senior Superintending Veterinary Inspector of the National Disease Control Centre. She says that initially, there were significant mortalities reported when the virus first hit the Netherlands, but the impact has been less severe as the virus moved westwards across the UK. item.title: Two newly graduated Gardaí assigned to the Kerry Garda Division
item.description: Two newly graduated gardaí are to be assigned to the Kerry Garda Division. 167 new Gardaí became sworn members of the force today. The southern region will be assigned 21 trainees, including two to the Kerry Garda Division. Advertisement One of the newly sworn officers will be stationed in Tralee, while another is to be deployed in Killarney. item.title: Children’s Minister says she supports proposed Valerie’s Law
item.description: The Minister for Children says she supports the proposed Valerie’s Law legislation. Kerry Fianna Fáil TD Norma Foley was responding to calls made by David French on Radio Kerry. His sister Valerie was murdered by her husband James Kilroy in 2019; Mr French has lobbied the government to introduce Valerie’s Law. item.description: There are calls for the Minister for Enterprise to establish a taskforce for West Limerick following the announcement that there’ll be around 140 job losses at Kostal Abbeyfeale. It's understood that its decision to transfer production of on-board chargers from Abbeyfeale to China will occur in the last quarter of this year. item.title: Ipswich manager reveals reason for Szmodics loan
item.description: Ipswich Town manager Kieran McKenna says the decision to loan Republic of Ireland international Sammie Szmodics to Derby County was not based on football performance, but on maintaining dressing-room culture. Szmodics joined Derby on loan until the end of the season on deadline day, having scored once for Ipswich this campaign after returning from a long-term ankle injury. item.title: INMO says bed management plan needed to ensure Kerry patients can be cared for locally
item.description: There needs to be a plan around bed management when transferring patients from hospital to other care settings in Kerry. That’s according to West Kerry native Phil Ní Sheaghdha, who is general secretary of the Irish Nurses’ and Midwives’ Organisation. She met with members of the Kerry INMO branch last night where this issue was discussed. Advertisement Ms Ní Sheaghdha says some patients are being moved from hospital to other care settings in the opposite end of the county, far from their homes.

item.title: SIPTU expresses shock and anger at scale of redundancies sought at Kostal Abbeyfeale plant
item.description: The trade union SIPTU has expressed shock and anger at the scale of redundancies sought by management of the Kostal Abbeyfeale plant. Kostal is a major employer in West Limerick and North Kerry, but last night it was confirmed up to 140 jobs will be lost at the Abbeyfeale facility. The redundancies follow Kostal’s decision to transfer the production of on-board chargers from Abbeyfeale to China, which it’s understood will occur in the last quarter of this year. item.title: 63 new jobs were created in Kerry’s Gaeltacht regions last year
item.description: 63 new jobs were created in Kerry’s Gaeltacht regions last year. That’s according to Údarás na Gaeltachta’s end of year statement for 2025. It shows over 9,700 (9,716) people are employed in Údarás client companies. Advertisement This includes 911 employees in the Gaeltacht areas of Uíbh Ráthach and Daingean Uí Chúis, a 2% drop in a year. The report shows four vacancies are available with client companies within the Kerry Gaeltacht regions.
